a:r.a:t: Lead with the Vault subscription. The Vault is $5.99 per month instead of $8 per month. Attendees who register on Saturday receive one bonus month. Then briefly explain that the subscription makes three Will options available: the Basic Will Template is free, Premium Individual is $275 instead of $350, and Premium Family is $500 for two applications instead of $700.

Explain that grief is often followed immediately by practical questions. Use: “Often, all of that information exists in one place: in the person’s head.” Then: “Estate planning is about making things easier for the people you love.”

Open with the question and pause. “Most of us spend our lives taking care of our families. Very few of us prepare them for the one moment when we may no longer be there to answer their questions.” Then briefly introduce The Muslim Will. Do not discuss the offer or pricing yet.
Establish the Will as essential, but not the entire solution. Keep the Islamic point concise. Transition: “That is why we built The Muslim Will.”
Explain the process quickly. The purpose is to remove complexity. Then: “The Will is where the journey starts. It is not where it ends.”
This is the pivot. Ask the four questions slowly. Then: “A Will gives direction. The family still needs the information around it.” Move directly into the Vault reveal.

Describe the Vault as a living estate record. Explain that assets, accounts, obligations and documents change over time. The Vault stays useful because the customer can keep it current. This is the rational reason for the subscription.

Do not read the slide. Use the four questions as the story. Spend more time on Voice & Video Library. Explain that some things do not belong in a legal document: advice, a story, an explanation or a message in your own voice.

Make the direct ask. “Do not leave this as something you will think about someday. Take out your phone and scan the QR code. Start by activating your Vault. You will receive the bonus month, and if you need a Will, your subscription unlocks today’s event pricing.” Leave this slide on screen throughout Q&A.
Compare the two experiences. “Both people created a Will. One left instructions. The other left instructions and organization.” Then: “Do not just leave a Will. Leave clarity.”
Widen the market. Make clear that the Vault is useful whether the attendee already has a Will, needs one, or is not ready to create one yet. The primary action for everyone is activating the Vault.
